sequence_before_fix: artifact = build_recovery_artifact(...)  # computes and stamps artifact_sha256/artifact_identity via content_identity()
artifact["operational_summary"]["HISTORY_RECOVERY_RUNTIME"] = diagnostic  # mutates the payload AFTER identity was already finalized
output.write_text(json.dumps(artifact, ...))  # persists a payload whose bytes no longer match its own stored artifact_sha256
confirmed_root_cause.why_downstream_fails_closed: market_wide_current_descriptive_research.build_artifact() calls content_identity(technical_history_recovery_artifact) (a generic whole-payload hash over every key except artifact_sha256/artifact_identity) and compares it to the stored artifact_sha256. Because HISTORY_RECOVERY_RUNTIME was added after that hash was computed, the fresh recomputation always disagrees with the stored value for every --all run.
confirmed_root_cause.scope_of_defect: Only the --all (run_all) orchestration path is affected. The --batch/--consolidate path (run_batch + consolidate) never adds HISTORY_RECOVERY_RUNTIME at all, so it was never exposed to this mutation-after-identity bug (a separate, pre-existing shape inconsistency between the two paths, out of scope for this corrective milestone).

Verified the test fails against the pre-fix code (temporarily set aside via a tagged git stash, then reapplied) with a genuine stored-vs-recomputed hash mismatch, then passes against the corrected code.
